verses.pali: Aṅguttara Nikāya 3.123
verses.english: Numbered Discourses 3.123

verses.pali: 13. Kusināravagga
verses.english: 13. Kusinārā

verses.pali: Kusinārasutta
verses.english: At Kusinārā

verses.pali: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā kusinārāyaṁ viharati baliharaṇe vanasaṇḍe.
verses.english: At one time the Buddha was staying near Kusinārā, in the Forest of Offerings.

verses.pali: Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi:
verses.english: There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,

verses.pali: “bhikkhavo”ti.
verses.english: “Mendicants!”

verses.pali: “Bhadante”ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṁ.
verses.english: “Venerable sir,” they replied.

verses.pali: Bhagavā etadavoca:
verses.english: The Buddha said this:

verses.pali: “Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu aññataraṁ gāmaṁ vā nigamaṁ vā upanissāya viharati.
verses.english: “Mendicants, take the case of a mendicant living supported by a town or village.

verses.pali: Tamenaṁ gahapati vā gahapatiputto vā upasaṅkamitvā svātanāya bhattena nimanteti.
verses.english: A householder or their child approaches and invites them for the next day’s meal.

verses.pali: Ākaṅkhamāno, bhikkhave, bhikkhu adhivāseti.
verses.english: The mendicant accepts if they want.

verses.pali: So tassā rattiyā accayena pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena tassa gahapatissa vā gahapatiputtassa vā nivesanaṁ tenupasaṅkamati; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdati.
verses.english: When the night has passed, they robe up in the morning, take their bowl and robe, and approach that householder’s home, where they sit on the seat spread out.

verses.pali: Tamenaṁ so gahapati vā gahapatiputto vā paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappeti sampavāreti.
verses.english: The householder or their child serves and satisfies them with their own hands with delicious fresh and cooked foods.

verses.pali: Tassa evaṁ hoti:
verses.english: The mendicant thinks:

verses.pali: ‘sādhu vata myāyaṁ gahapati vā gahapatiputto vā paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappeti sampavāretī’ti.
verses.english: ‘It’s so good that this householder serves me with delicious fresh and cooked foods.’

verses.pali: Evampissa hoti:
verses.english: Then they think:

verses.pali: ‘aho vata māyaṁ gahapati vā gahapatiputto vā āyatimpi evarūpena paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappeyya sampavāreyyā’ti.
verses.english: ‘I really hope this householder serves me with delicious fresh and cooked foods in the future, too.’

verses.pali: So taṁ piṇḍapātaṁ gathito mucchito ajjhosanno anādīnavadassāvī anissaraṇapañño paribhuñjati.
verses.english: They eat that food tied, infatuated, attached, blind to the drawbacks, and not understanding the escape.

verses.pali: So tattha kāmavitakkampi vitakketi, byāpādavitakkampi vitakketi, vihiṁsāvitakkampi vitakketi.
verses.english: They think about it with sensual, malicious, or cruel thoughts.

verses.pali: Evarūpassāhaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno dinnaṁ na mahapphalanti vadāmi.
verses.english: A gift to such a mendicant is not very fruitful, I say.

verses.pali: Taṁ kissa hetu?
verses.english: Why is that?

verses.pali: Pamatto hi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu viharati.
verses.english: Because that mendicant is negligent.

verses.pali: Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu aññataraṁ gāmaṁ vā nigamaṁ vā upanissāya viharati.
verses.english: Take another case of a mendicant living supported by a town or village.

verses.pali: Tamenaṁ gahapati vā gahapatiputto vā upasaṅkamitvā svātanāya bhattena nimanteti.
verses.english: A householder or their child approaches and invites them for the next day’s meal.

verses.pali: Ākaṅkhamāno, bhikkhave, bhikkhu adhivāseti.
verses.english: The mendicant accepts if they want.

verses.pali: So tassā rattiyā accayena pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena tassa gahapatissa vā gahapatiputtassa vā nivesanaṁ tenupasaṅkamati; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdati.
verses.english: When the night has passed, they robe up in the morning, take their bowl and robe, and approach that householder’s home, where they sit on the seat spread out.

verses.pali: Tamenaṁ so gahapati vā gahapatiputto vā paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappeti sampavāreti.
verses.english: The householder or their child serves and satisfies them with their own hands with delicious fresh and cooked foods.

verses.pali: Tassa na evaṁ hoti:
verses.english: It never occurs to them:

verses.pali: ‘sādhu vata myāyaṁ gahapati vā gahapatiputto vā paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappeti sampavāretī’ti.
verses.english: ‘It’s so good that the householder or their child serves and satisfies me with their own hands with delicious fresh and cooked foods.’

verses.pali: Evampissa na hoti:
verses.english: They don’t think:

verses.pali: ‘aho vata māyaṁ gahapati vā gahapatiputto vā āyatimpi evarūpena paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappeyya sampavāreyyā’ti.
verses.english: ‘I really hope this householder serves me with delicious fresh and cooked foods in the future, too.’

verses.pali: So taṁ piṇḍapātaṁ agathito amucchito anajjhosanno ādīnavadassāvī nissaraṇapañño paribhuñjati.
verses.english: They eat that almsfood untied, uninfatuated, unattached, seeing the drawback, and understanding the escape.

verses.pali: So tattha nekkhammavitakkampi vitakketi, abyāpādavitakkampi vitakketi, avihiṁsāvitakkampi vitakketi.
verses.english: They think about it with thoughts of renunciation, good will, or harmlessness.

verses.pali: Evarūpassāhaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno dinnaṁ mahapphalanti vadāmi.
verses.english: A gift to such a mendicant is very fruitful, I say.

verses.pali: Taṁ kissa hetu?
verses.english: Why is that?

verses.pali: Appamatto hi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu viharatī”ti.
verses.english: Because that mendicant is diligent.”

verses.pali: Paṭhamaṁ.
